h1: European-style (Amada-Promecam) press brake punches — straight, acute, gooseneck, same-height, radius and offset tools
intro: EUROSTAMP punches for press brakes with European-style clamping — the Amada-Promecam standard used by Amada and Promecam and by dozens of other makers, from Accurpress, Baykal and Dener to Durmazlar, Ermaksan, Prima Power, Salvagnini and Yawei. Made in Italy from C45 and 42CrMo4 steel, induction-hardened to 55 – 60 HRC on the working surfaces, in 835 mm (32.9″) and 415 mm (16.3″) lengths and 805 mm (31.7″) sectioned sets with horns. Six families on this page: straight punches from 45° to 88° and heavy-duty punches with R6 – R10 tips for plate; acute 24° to 35° punches; gooseneck and sash punches for return flanges; the ESH series with one 120 mm working height for staged bending; radius holders with round elements R3 to R50; and offset (joggle) tools. The punches link to their DXF profiles for your CNC, and NovoTech quotes, ships and supports the tooling from Mississauga, ON, Canada.

faq.q: Will these punches fit my press brake?
faq.a: If your press brake clamps European-style (Amada-Promecam) tooling, yes. EUROSTAMP lists Amada, Promecam, Accurpress, Adira, Baykal, Boschert, Bystronic-Beyeler Euro-B, Colgar, Dener, Durmazlar, Ermaksan, Gasparini, Haco, Prima Power, Salvagnini, Yawei and many more as using this style. If you are not sure, send us a photo of the upper clamp and a punch you use now — or the model of the brake — and we confirm before you order. Adapters let other press brakes take these punches.

A straight punch is stiffer and carries more load, so it is the first choice for open angles and plate. A gooseneck is relieved behind the tip: use it when a flange you have already bent comes back towards the punch — U-channels, pans, boxes with return flanges. The deeper the neck, the lower the load rating, so check the table before you bend thick plate on a gooseneck.

faq.q: What tip radius should I choose?
faq.a: In air bending the inside radius is set mostly by the V opening — about 1/6 of the V in mild steel — not by the punch. Choose a punch radius at or below that natural radius: R0.6 to R0.8 for sheet up to about 10 gauge, R1.5 to R3 for 3/16 to 1/4″, and the heavy-duty R6 – R10 punches for plate thicker than about 3/8″, where a sharp tip would crack the outside of the bend. A sharp R0.25 punch gives crisp corners in thin stainless and aluminum.

faq.q: What are horns and sectioned sets?
faq.a: A sectioned set is a punch or die cut into pieces that add up to a standard length — for European-style punches 805 mm (31.7″) made of 100 mm horns at each end and 10, 15, 20, 40, 50, 200 and 270 mm pieces. You assemble the exact length of a bend, and the horns — the ends relieved on the outside — let you bend the sides of a box without hitting the flanges already formed.

ESH stands for EUROSTAMP Same Height: every punch in the series — straight, gooseneck, sash, 86°, 60°, 30° and 26° — has the same 120 mm working height, and the matching insert dies the same 60 mm. Several tools can be set up side by side in stations and used without re-setting the ram, which saves set-up time on parts with several different bends.

faq.q: Can we get the tools as DXF files for our CNC?
faq.a: Yes — every tool in these tables that has a DXF link can be downloaded straight from the page: the profile drawn in millimetres, ready to import into the tool library of a Delem, ESA or Cybelec control or into offline bending software. For the few tools without one, ask us and we get the drawing from EUROSTAMP.
